note: Original description (Eutermes lujae), in German. The scan OCR contains several misreadings (e.g. 14 segments read as 'r4', '19'), the segment counts and measurements having been checked against the context and recorded as they stand.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: (Placed in Eutermes in the original, Nasutus type.) A single size class. Total length 3.2 mm, head including mandibles 1.2 mm. Very similar to E. ferranti, but: head broader and more spherical; nasus measured from the antennal bases only as long as the head; nasus distinctly narrower, more strongly contracted at the base and only slightly tapering from base to tip. Head colour also paler, red-yellow with a brown nasus. Antennal segment count quite different from E. ferranti: segment 3 much longer, equal to the sum of segments 2 and 4, segment 4 slightly shorter than segment 2, segment 2 slightly longer than wide; antennae sometimes not fully 14-segmented, segment 3 then slightly constricted in the middle. Antennae with yellow rings, as long as head plus nasus, hardly thickening towards the tip; segment 4 as long as wide, segment 5 slightly longer than wide, the following segments slightly larger, the last 4 about 1.5 times as long as wide. Anterior lobe of the pronotum truncate in the middle of the anterior margin, with a very small, almost dot-like but distinct notch, this notch absent in E. ferranti.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Major worker: body length 4 mm. Head brown with white markings, a flat oval white fontanelle depression in the middle of the frons, the anterior part of the frons slightly concave, postclypeus strongly convex, almost semicircular, only 3 times as wide as long. Anterior lobe of the pronotum with a small notch in the middle. Antennae 14-segmented, as long as the head, with yellow rings, thickening towards the tip. Minor worker: body length 3—3.5 mm, head relatively smaller, paler ivory yellow with white markings, postclypeus 4 times as wide as long. Otherwise as in the major worker. The two worker forms differ from the 3 mm long worker of E. ferranti chiefly in the postclypeus of the latter being 6 times as wide as long.

sections.label: Nymph
sections.text: Body length 6 mm, width 2 mm, white, with brown patches on the sides of the occiput, the margin of the pronotum brown, short brown wing pads present, the margins of the abdominal segments brown; frons with an elongate white fontanelle depression; antennae slightly longer than the head, slightly thick, 15-segmented, segment 3 very short and almost inseparable from segment 4, segments 4 and 5 also very short and ring-like, the following segments gradually longer, segments 14 and 15 longer than wide.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: King body length 6 mm, dark brown, head black, densely covered with yellow-grey hairs except on the head; head large and circular, coriaceous-rugose and glossy. It differs from E. maculiventris Sjöstedt in the much smaller body, the nasus and head colour clearly different, the much longer antennal segment 3 and the non-arcuate anterior margin of the pronotum; from E. comorensis Wasmann in the narrower head, longer nasus, longer antennal segment 3 and the anterior margin of the anterior pronotal lobe bearing only a minute dot-like notch. Locality: Belgian Congo.
